title: Answering a Standing Claim Hold on a Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
The standing claim hold on a Keyturn Host Payout Account is every reserve taken against an open claim on the account, less every reserve already freed from it, rounded half to even to two decimal places. How much of that standing hold the settlement money answers turns on the correcting entries booked to the account and on whether its transfers have been coming back.

| The correcting entries booked to the account | Transfers come back unpaid in the last twelve months | What is answered |
|---|---|---|
| Meet or exceed the standing claim hold | 1 or fewer | The whole standing hold |
| Fall short of the standing claim hold | 1 or fewer | Only as much of the hold as those correcting entries come to |
| Any | 2 or more | Only the excess of the correcting entries over the standing hold, and never less than nothing |

The tolerated number of returns is 1, so an account with no return and an account with exactly 1 return in the last twelve months both sit in the first two rows, while an account with 2 returns in that period falls to the third whatever the correcting entries show.

## Both sides of each boundary

On a hypothetical standing claim hold of 5000.00 USD with correcting entries of 5000.00 USD and no return in the last twelve months, the first row governs, since the entries meet the hold, and the whole 5000.00 USD is answered. With correcting entries of 4999.00 USD and the same return record, the second row governs and 4999.00 USD is answered. With correcting entries of 5000.00 USD and 2 returns in that period, the third row governs and the excess is nothing, so nothing is answered.

## Where the records stand

The standing claim hold is read from the reserve entries on the account that carry an open claim as their ground and from the releases already booked against them; the correcting entries are the corrections booked to the same account; and the returns are the returned transfers booked to it in the twelve months up to that day.
